regimens.indication: Idiopathic, Arteriosclerotic, and Postencephalitic Parkinsonism — Adults

refs.quote: Trihexyphenidyl is indicated as an adjunct in the treatment of all forms of parkinsonism (postencephalitic, arteriosclerotic, and idiopathic).

As initial therapy for parkinsonism, 1 mg of trihexyphenidyl hydrochloride may be administered the first day. The dose may then be increased by 2 mg increments at intervals of three to five days, until a total of 6 to 10 mg is given daily.

dose.frequency: once daily initially, titrated to 3-4 divided doses daily

regimens.dose_text: Initial: 1 mg PO on Day 1; increase by 2 mg increments every 3 to 5 days to 6 to 10 mg daily (postencephalitic parkinsonism may require 12 to 15 mg daily). Divide into 3 doses with meals (4 doses if >10 mg/day, 4th at bedtime). Avoid abrupt withdrawal.

refs.quote: The total daily dosage usually ranges between 5 and 15 mg although, in some cases, these reactions have been satisfactorily controlled with as little as 1 mg daily. It may be advisable to commence therapy with a single 1 mg dose.

dose.frequency: initial single dose, titrated empirically (usual 5-15 mg/day)

regimens.dose_text: Commence with a single 1 mg PO dose; if extrapyramidal manifestations are not controlled in a few hours, progressively increase subsequent doses empirically. Usual total daily dosage ranges between 5 and 15 mg (some controlled on 1 mg/day). Consider reducing tranquilizer dose temporarily.

refs.locator: DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION - Concomitant Use with Levodopa
refs.quote: When trihexyphenidyl is used concomitantly with levodopa, the usual dose of each may need to be reduced. Careful adjustment is necessary, depending on side effects and degree of symptom control. A trihexyphenidyl dosage of 3 to 6 mg daily, in divided doses, is usually adequate.

dose.frequency: daily in divided doses (3 to 6 mg/day)

regimens.dose_text: When used concomitantly with levodopa, 3 to 6 mg PO daily in divided doses is usually adequate; usual doses of both trihexyphenidyl and levodopa may need reduction based on side effects and symptom control.

refs.quote: The initial dose should be low and then increased gradually, especially in patients over 60 years of age.

Sensitivity to the actions of parasympatholytic drugs may increase with age, particularly over the age of 60; therefore, elderly patients generally should be started on low doses of trihexyphenidyl and observed closely.

dose.frequency: once daily initially, increased gradually with close observation

regimens.dose_text: Start with low initial dose (e.g., 1 mg daily) and increase gradually with close observation in patients >60 years due to increased sensitivity to parasympatholytic effects.

value.drug_or_class: Central Nervous System Depressants, Alcohol, Cannabinoids & Opiates
value.effect: Additive central nervous system depressant and sedative effects, with potential for impairment and substance misuse.
value.management: Warn patients regarding excessive sedation; avoid alcohol and monitor closely if coadministered with sedative medications.

refs.quote: Cannabinoids, barbiturates, opiates, and alcohol may have additive effects with trihexyphenidyl, and thus, an abuse potential exists.

value.effect: Additive anticholinergic effects precipitating paralytic ileus, narrow-angle glaucoma exacerbation, or toxic confusional states.
value.management: Monitor for enhanced anticholinergic toxicity; dose reduction of one or both agents may be required.

refs.quote: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors and tricyclic antidepressants possessing significant anticholinergic activity may intensify the anticholinergic effects of antidyskinetic agents because of the secondary anticholinergic activities of these medications.
